text:
maia (People Ops Lead): Thanks everyone for joining the all-hands Q&A earlier. I'm consolidating follow-ups here — will keep it short and actionable. TL;DR: promo window opens 2026-04-01, managers submit calibrations by 2026-04-20, final decisions early May. Reply here with any edge cases you want tracked.

jamal (Eng Manager): Quick clarifying Q — are exceptions for mid-cycle promotions still allowed (e.g., fast track for startup hires)?

maia (People Ops Lead): Yes — exceptions allowed but need manager + director signoff and a short justification (1-2 bullets). Use the exception label on the submit template. We review those during calibration week.

sanjay (IC3): For level moves, is the rubric the same as last year? Any change to expectations for IC4?

maia (People Ops Lead): Rubrics are unchanged in intent, but we updated examples for IC4 scope to include cross-org ownership. See the rubric doc: https://redwood-inference.internal/docs/leveling/rubrics. If you want a quick call to walk through one candidate, ping me.

jamal (Eng Manager): Also—how does retroactive pay work if promotion is effective Apr 1 but comp approvals lag until May?

alex (Finance): Retro pay is supported when comp approvals are documented before payroll cutoffs. Normal process: effective date = promo date, retro paid in the next payroll cycle after approval. If approvals are delayed >30 days, we'll flag with payroll and handle on a case-by-case basis.

maia (People Ops Lead): Adding timeline snippet so it's clear:
```
promo_window_start: 2026-04-01
manager_submit_by: 2026-04-20
calibration_meet_range: 2026-04-25 - 2026-04-30
comp_signoff_by: 2026-05-07
payroll_retro_target: next_pay_after_approval
```

sanjay (IC3): What about people who were on parental leave during review period — do they need manager self-nom?

maia (People Ops Lead): No, managers should nominate people who were on leave. We have an accommodations guideline in the doc that ensures people on leave aren't disadvantaged. If you hit an exception, mark `leave-accommodation` on the row.

jamal (Eng Manager): Is there a public template for manager submissions? I couldn't find it in Confluence.

people-ops-bot: Uploaded file: submit_calibration_template.csv -> https://files.redwood-inference.internal/submit_calibration_template.csv :file_folder:

maia (People Ops Lead): ^ use that CSV. Required columns: employee_name, current_level, proposed_level, justification_2bullets, tenure_months, comp_band_impact, exception_label (optional).

alex (Finance): One more note on comp bands: Finance is proposing a minor band refresh to align to market comps. Any changes would be communicated before comp signoff — nothing will be applied retroactively for offers already extended.

sanjay (IC3): 401k matching question from the AMA — is the proposed 401k match change finalized?

maia (People Ops Lead): We are moving to a phased 401k match increase, details to HR portal this week. Short version: match moves from 4% to 5% phased starting 2026-07-01 (applies after 90 days of eligibility). Will post an FAQ doc later today.

jamal (Eng Manager): Thanks. One last ask — can People Ops share the calibration schedule so managers can block time?

maia (People Ops Lead): Yep — preach. Calendar invites will go out by EOD tomorrow with 30-min slots for each manager + one 1-hour team block for director-level decisions. If you need a custom slot, DM me.

maia (People Ops Lead): If anyone has confidential cases, DM me or use the `people-ops-confidential` channel with `@maia`. I'll keep this thread for public clarifications. Thanks all :thumbsup:
